title: Cohomology of RHom(M,-) is Hom in the derived category, compatibly with connecting maps
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with enough injectives [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $M$ be an object of $\mathcal A$, let $v=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,-):\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}$ (left exact and additive [def-sp-left-exact-additive]) and let $Rv:D^+(\mathcal A)\to D^+(\mathrm{Ab})$ be its right derived functor [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories], computed on $X$ by a quasi-isomorphism $\varepsilon:X\to I$ to a bounded below complex of injectives as $Rv(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,I^\bullet)$ [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. Then for every $X\in D^+(\mathcal A)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ there is an isomorphism $\psi^n_X:H^n(Rv(X))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],X[n])$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sending the class of a cocycle $f:M\to I^n$ (read as a morphism of complexes $M[0]\to I[n]$) to $(\varepsilon[n])^{-1}\circ f$, independent of the choice of $I$ and natural in $X$. Moreover, for every distinguished triangle $X\to Y\to Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ of $D^+(\mathcal A)$, with $\delta^n:H^n(Rv(Z))\to H^{n+1}(Rv(X))$ the homology connecting maps [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] of the distinguished triangle $Rv(X)\to Rv(Y)\to Rv(Z)\to Rv(X)[1]$, one has $\psi^{n+1}_X\circ\delta^n=(w[n]\circ-)\circ\psi^n_Z$, where $w[n]\circ-:\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],Z[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],X[n+1])$ is the connecting map of the homological functor $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],-)$ [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle].

proof.text: Let $\varepsilon:X\to I^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism to a bounded below complex of injectives, so $Rv(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,I^\bullet)$ by the bridge [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]; $I^\bullet$ is K-injective [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], hence so is $I^\bullet[n]$ (its terms are again injective and it is bounded below). A degree-$n$ cocycle $f:M\to I^n$ ($d^nf=0$) is exactly a morphism of complexes $f:M[0]\to I^\bullet[n]$, and $f=d^{n-1}g$ with $g:M\to I^{n-1}$ exactly when $f$ is homotopic to zero (homotopy $\pm g$, the sign being that of the differential of $I[n]$); so $H^n(Rv(X))=\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(M[0],I^\bullet[n])$. The localization bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] for the K-injective complex $I^\bullet[n]$ identifies this with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],I^\bullet[n])$, and composing with the isomorphism $(\varepsilon[n])^{-1}$ of $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $\psi^n_X$, an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06XR (derived-lemma-compute-ext-resolutions), part (1), together with Tag 070I (K-injective localization)

proof.text: The construction is independent of the chosen resolution and natural in $X$: a morphism $g:X\to X'$ of $D^+(\mathcal A)$ is, by the localization bijection [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] for the K-injective $I_{X'}$ [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], represented by a unique homotopy class of morphisms of complexes $\tilde g:I_X\to I_{X'}$ with $\tilde g\circ\varepsilon=\varepsilon'\circ g$ in $D(\mathcal A)$, and $Rv(g)$ is $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,\tilde g)$ [def-sp-kinjective-bridge]. For a cocycle $f$ the class $H^n(Rv(g))[f]=[\tilde g^nf]$ is sent by $\psi^n_{X'}$ to $(\varepsilon'[n])^{-1}\circ\tilde g[n]\circ f=g[n]\circ(\varepsilon[n])^{-1}\circ f$ (the shift of a morphism of complexes has components $\tilde g[n]^r=\tilde g^{r+n}$, no sign [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]); that is, $\psi^n_{X'}\circ H^n(Rv(g))=(g[n]\circ-)\circ\psi^n_X$. With $g=\mathrm{id}_X$ and two resolutions this is the independence of $I$.

source.place: Tag 070I, K-injective resolutions and uniqueness of lifts up to homotopy

proof.text: Let $X\to Y\to Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1]$ be distinguished in $D^+(\mathcal A)$. Choosing $I_X[1]$ as the resolution of $X[1]$, the right derived functor is triangulated with shift isomorphism $\sigma_X:Rv(X[1])=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(M,I_X[1])=Rv(X)[1]$ the identity (the differential of both is $-\operatorname{Hom}(M,d)$), so the image triangle $Rv(X)\to Rv(Y)\to Rv(Z)\xrightarrow{Rv(w)}Rv(X)[1]$ is distinguished [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Its homology connecting map [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] is, by the definition of that map (in the Mathlib leaf `DerivedCategory.HomologySequence.δ`, the shifted $H^0$ of the third morphism), $\delta^n=H^n(Rv(w))$ followed by the identification $H^n(Rv(X)[1])=H^{n+1}(Rv(X))$, which is the identity on cocycles since $(K[1])^n=K^{n+1}$ with differential $-d$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Likewise $\psi^n_{X[1]}$ computed with $I_X[1]$ equals $\psi^{n+1}_X$, because $(I_X[1])[n]=I_X[n+1]$ as complexes (both differentials are $(-1)^{n+1}d$). Step 2 for $g=w:Z\to X[1]$ now gives $\psi^{n+1}_X\circ\delta^n=\psi^n_{X[1]}\circ H^n(Rv(w))=(w[n]\circ-)\circ\psi^n_Z$. Finally, for the homological functor $\Phi=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal A)}(M[0],-)$, the map $\Phi(Z[n])\to\Phi(X[n+1])$ of [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle] is $\Phi(w[n])=w[n]\circ-$. No sign enters: the cone triangle already carries $-p$ (Stacks convention, [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]), and neither shifting morphisms nor $\sigma$ introduces one.
